chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Bob Fuller: dance school, jail turnkey and clarinet limits
summary: Bob Fuller later worked at the Dreamland Dance School and became a city jail turnkey; Dance and Caldwell judge his clarinet amateurish.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I mean now, where did Bob Fuller come from?

Well, I was asked by the club I belonged to, oldest Negre the only musicians' club in the country, and he was a member of that club for years, and last time I saw Bob was after the war, and we were always good friends, buddies, and Bob had left -- after he left the dancing school, he had a job for years playing on 125th Street, called the Dreamland Dance School, a dance school where they had these hostesses like, and anyway in all Bob was there about ten or 12 years. So when that place closed up because the gangsters
controlling it, he taken an examination, and last time I saw him he was a turnkey at the city jail. He worked for the police department.

Oh, that's a switch. Well, why I was curious where he came from was, now, I've heard him on records. Now, he never seemed to -- he never seemed to have got with that clarinet, like, you know, the New Orleans and the guys at Chicago. He didn't seem to have the -- I mean there was something lacking there.
Yes, there was. He didn't have -- he hadn't got to that medium where, you know, followed through to where the guys were swinging or playing Dixieland or --
Yeah, he sounded -- he really sounded a little bit amateur.
Yeah, he never could reach that thing. I don't know what it was, but --
But he made a lot of records.
Made a lot of records, yes, he did, whole lot of records.
